hook: The German princess who seized the Russian throne and ruled for 34 years.

pages.x: She was born Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst in 1729, a minor German princess. At 14 she was chosen as a bride for Peter, heir to the Russian throne. She learned Russian, joined the Orthodox Church and took the name Catherine.
Her husband played with toy soldiers and worshipped Prussia, Russia's enemy. Catherine read Voltaire and Montesquieu, and made friends among the palace guards.

In 1762, six months after Peter became tsar, she led a coup with the guards, riding at their head in a guards uniform. Peter was forced to give up the throne and was killed days later, probably by her supporters.
She ruled for 34 years. Her armies beat the Ottomans and won Crimea and the Black Sea coast, and with Prussia and Austria she carved up Poland until it vanished from the map.
Her favourite and general, Potemkin, led her on a grand tour of Crimea in 1787. A legend says he set up fake villages along the route to impress her. A "Potemkin village" still means a fake front.

She bought whole collections of paintings from across Europe, wrote to Voltaire and Diderot, and bought Diderot's library. Her collection became the Hermitage Museum, one of the greatest in the world.
She talked of reform, but the lives of Russia's serfs grew harder under her. In 1773 the Cossack Pugachev led a huge peasant revolt. It was crushed, and he was executed in Moscow.
Catherine pushed Russia to the Black Sea and made it a great European power. A patron of art and the Enlightenment, she is the longest-ruling woman in Russian history.
pts: Expanded Russia to the Black Sea
